title: Grateful Dead Live at Kezar Stadium on 1973-05-26
lineage: Dat -> CD -> Samplitude Professional v9.02 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat D

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear Charlie Miller soundboard capture of a marathon three‑set Kezar show with smoking “They Love Each Other”, “Playin’ In The Band” and an epic “Truckin’ > Other One > Eyes” sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a superbly mastered 1973 soundboard tape, praised for its crispness, excellent stereo guitar separation and virtually no clutter, with only occasional buzz that most listeners miss. Musically the performance ranks among the year’s best – three high‑energy sets packed with standout moments like “They Love Each Other”, “Playin’ In The Band”, “Truckin’ > Other One > Eyes” and a tight “China Cat > Rider”.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly enthusiastic reviews praise both the show’s musical brilliance and the recording’s pristine sound; only a handful of minor complaints about buzz keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with superb stereo panning (Jerry right, Bob left). Reviewers note near‑perfect clarity and balance; a few mention an occasional low‑level buzz or bass clipping that is mostly inaudible on speakers.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set marathon that builds from a warm‑up first set into a high‑energy second and an exploratory third; the pacing stays engaging despite a few early‑show glitches.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Front‑and‑center with flawless tone; his solos on “They Love Each Other” and “Playin' In The Band” are highlighted as exceptional.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as “ultrabass wizardry”; Phil’s lines in the “Other One/Eyes” sequence receive high praise.
band_member_comments.Bob: Stereo separation puts his rhythm guitar on the far left, noted as clear and powerful; one reviewer calls him a phenomenal guitarist.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith works a solid piano/Rhodes blend, praised on “Big River”, “El Paso” and “Box of Rain”; a couple of reviewers wish he were a bit louder in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming is consistently described as tight and energetic, supporting the long jams without issue.
